result.title: Towards Field-Deployable Wearable IMU Systems for Occupational Activity Recognition
result.summary: Wearable inertial measurement unit (IMU) systems for construction worker human activity recognition (HAR) routinely report aggregate accuracies above 95 %, rarely under genuine subject-independent (leave-one-subject-out (LOSO)) evaluation, masking the per-individual variance that determines real-world deployment performance. Using the VTT-ConIoT benchmark, we conduct, to our knowledge, the first systematic configuration sensitivity analysis of this dataset: six classifiers across five sensor placements and three window sizes under a single LOSO protocol, a personalised-calibration pilot, and a validated comparison of tabular GAN-based and standard time-series augmentation. Per-subject LOSO accuracy for the main multi-sensor, 16-class configuration ranges from 61.9 % to 88.7 % (mean 77.5 %), a 27 pp spread, though all data are laboratory-collected. Multi-sensor fusion and longer windows both improve accuracy; standard augmentation gives small, consistent gains, while Conditional Tabular GAN (CTGAN) augmentation actively harms accuracy with a demonstrated distributional-fidelity mechanism; and personalised calibration recovers 16.8 pp for the weakest participants from just 30 % of their own data. These findings provide evidence-grounded configuration guidance for scaling occupational body sensor networks towards field deployment

AI.brief_summary: 该论文在 VTT-ConIoT 可穿戴 IMU 基准上系统比较分类器、传感器位置、窗口大小与数据增强策略，并检验个体化校准的效果，指出主体独立（LOSO）评估下职业活动识别精度存在显著个体间差异。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究属惯性传感器的人体活动识别与部署配置分析，不涉及视觉或多模态推理的内部状态、证据筛选与停止决策，个体化校准与 CTGAN 增强也未提供可迁移到 LVR 的具体方法线索，故排除。
